rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the primary uncertainty is the performance floor: what can a simple single-modality model achieve? config_014 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest, most interpretable RNA baseline available. It establishes a clean reference point with minimal confounding (no image modality, no learned encoder, no aggregation/fusion), so any future improvement can be attributed to specific design choices (better RNA encoder, adding image modality, multiprofile, aggregation, fusion). Starting from this floor is the most information-efficient first step: it calibrates expectations, confirms the pipeline works, and provides the anchor against which all subsequent multimodal and multiprofile experiments will be judged. Under a limited budget, a clean baseline is more valuable than an early gamble on a complex configuration whose gains cannot yet be decomposed.

Evidence: The only completed experiment (config_014: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) yields ~48.5% validation accuracy, giving a single baseline but leaving the central question of the study unanswered—does adding image information improve multimodal cellular profiling? Uncertainty: We have no data on whether image features contribute any signal, making it impossible to prioritize among the many multimodal configurations. Question tested: config_006 keeps the RNA encoder (pca_n2000), profile setting (singleprofile), and aggregation (none) identical to config_014, adding only an imagenet_vit_l image encoder and a simple concat fusion. This isolates the effect of the image modality with minimal confounds. Why this is the best next experiment: With a limited budget and only one data point, the highest-value question is whether the second modality is worth pursuing at all. A positive result justifies investing further in image encoder choice, aggregation, and fusion; a null or negative result redirects effort toward RNA encoder variants and profile settings. Choosing the strongest available image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) maximizes the chance of detecting a true benefit, and concat is the simplest fusion, avoiding confounding from learned weighting.

Evidence: config_006 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, concat) achieves 0.535 acc, outperforming config_014 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) at 0.485 acc, confirming that adding the image modality with concat fusion provides a meaningful ~5% boost. Uncertainty: We have no evidence yet on whether multiprofile with aggregation improves over singleprofile. Question tested: config_024 is the minimal extension of config_006—same model setting, same RNA encoder (pca_n2000), same image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), same fusion (concat)—but switches to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation. This isolates the effect of multiprofile + simple averaging without confounding changes to encoders or fusion. Why best: It directly extends the current best configuration with the smallest possible change, making the result easy to attribute to the profile/aggregation decision. If it improves, we gain confidence that multiprofile is worth pursuing and can then test transformer aggregation or other encoders; if it does not, we avoid wasting budget on more complex multiprofile variants.

The current best (config_024: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat; acc 0.629) shows that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation provides a large gain over singleprofile (config_006, acc 0.535). The most natural and informative next step is to test whether a more expressive aggregation mechanism (transformer) can further improve over avgpool while holding all other design choices constant. config_013 differs from config_024 in exactly one variable (aggregation: avgpool → transformer), making it a clean single-factor comparison. If transformer outperforms avgpool, it signals that the aggregation architecture is a key lever and justifies further exploration of transformer-based designs; if it performs similarly or worse, it confirms that simple pooling is sufficient and redirects budget toward other dimensions (e.g., RNA encoder or fusion strategy). This maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: The current best (config_024, acc=0.629) uses pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder, and all four completed experiments share this encoder. We have strong evidence that multimodal + multiprofile + avgpool + concat + imagenet_vit_l is a promising backbone, but the RNA representation has been held constant. Uncertainty: It is unknown whether a learned, non-linear RNA encoder (scvi_n200) captures complementary or superior transcriptomic structure compared to PCA-2000, which is a linear dimensionality reduction. Question: config_049 changes exactly one variable relative to config_024 (rna_encoder: pca_n2000 → scvi_n200), isolating the effect of the RNA encoder while holding model setting, profile setting, image encoder, aggregation, and fusion fixed. Why best next: The RNA encoder is the most fundamental unexplored design axis; a clean single-variable test against the current best maximizes information per experiment. If scvi_n200 improves performance, it opens a productive direction (learned encoders); if it does not, it confirms PCA sufficiency and redirects budget toward other dimensions (e.g., fusion strategy or image encoder). This is more informative than testing a secondary knob like weighted fusion (config_001) because the representation choice is likely to have a larger and more structurally important effect.

Evidence: config_049 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) is the best at 0.715 acc, and with pca_n2000 we saw avgpool (0.629) outperform transformer (0.599) by ~3%. However, this aggregation comparison was only made with the weaker pca_n2000 encoder. Question: Does the aggregation choice (avgpool vs transformer) still matter when using the superior scvi_n200 representation, or does the richer latent space make the two strategies equivalent? This experiment (config_007) is a clean single-variable change from the best config—only swapping avgpool for transformer—so it isolates the aggregation effect under the current best RNA encoder. Why this is the best next experiment: it either confirms avgpool as the robust choice (letting us lock in aggregation and spend remaining budget on other dimensions like fusion or image encoder) or reveals that transformer aggregation interacts favorably with scvi_n200's richer representation, which would open a new optimization direction. Either outcome reduces uncertainty about a core design axis before we commit further experiments.

Evidence: The strongest signal is that scvi_n200 dramatically outperforms pca_n2000 (config_049: 0.715 vs config_024: 0.629), and the current best is config_007 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat, multiprofile) at 0.721 acc. All six completed experiments use concat fusion; the effect of fusion strategy in the high-performing scvi_n200 regime is completely untested. Question: config_017 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted while holding all other settings at their best-known values (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, multiprofile). This isolates the fusion effect as a single-variable comparison against config_007. Why this is the best next experiment: It is the cleanest exploitation of the current best direction—testing whether a learned fusion weighting can improve on simple concatenation without confounding the result with changes to encoder, aggregation, or profile setting. A positive result would yield an immediate performance gain; a null result would confirm concat sufficiency and redirect budget toward other unexplored axes (e.g., image encoder or scgpt).

Evidence: All completed experiments used imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder, so the image representation choice is completely unexplored. The RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) and profile setting (multi vs single) have been shown to matter substantially, but we have no information on whether a lighter image encoder (resnet50) is competitive or a bottleneck. Question: config_015 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) differs from config_049 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat, acc=0.715) in exactly one variable—the image encoder—making it a clean single-factor comparison. Why best next experiment: Under a limited budget, isolating the image encoder effect is critical because it determines whether we should continue investing in the larger ViT-L backbone or whether a simpler encoder suffices. If resnet50 is competitive, it tells us the image representation is not the current bottleneck and we should focus on RNA encoder (e.g., scgpt) or fusion details; if it degrades significantly, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential and justifies keeping it in all future configurations. This single experiment reduces uncertainty about a major untested design axis without confounding multiple changes.

The strongest evidence so far is that the RNA encoder choice is the dominant design variable: switching from PCA_n2000 to scvi_n200 (config_024→config_049) yielded a large ~8-point accuracy gain with all other settings held constant. The current best configuration (config_017: scvi_n200, ViT-L, transformer, weighted → 0.725 acc) has been reached, but scgpt has not been tested in any experiment. config_012 (scgpt, ViT-L, transformer, weighted) is a clean, single-variable swap against config_017, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder while keeping the image encoder, aggregation, and fusion at their best-performing values. This is the highest-information experiment available: if scgpt matches or exceeds scvi_n200, it opens a new promising direction; if it falls short, it confirms scvi_n200 as the preferred encoder and redirects budget toward refining aggregation/fusion or image-encoder choices. No other untested configuration addresses this critical, unexplored variable as directly.

The strongest evidence so far points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the best direction (0.715–0.725), but we lack a critical single-modality baseline: what does the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) achieve on its own with multiprofile and avgpool? Config_034 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool) directly isolates the image contribution using the same image encoder and aggregation as our best multimodal configs (e.g., config_049). If image-only approaches ~0.70, the RNA modality adds little and further multimodal tuning has limited upside; if it is substantially lower (e.g., ~0.55–0.60), RNA provides meaningful complementary signal and justifies continued multimodal exploration. This single experiment resolves the most important open design question—whether the multimodal fusion is genuinely additive or the image alone is near the ceiling—making it the highest-information-gain choice under a limited budget.
